titulo: Culture, festivals and traditions: Festivals, congratulations and wishes

aula.objetivo: Talk about festivals and customs with «se» and «soler», get to know some celebrations from Spain and Mexico, congratulate people and wish them well with «que + subjunctive», and compare traditions from your own country with those of Spanish-speaking countries.

blocos.titulo: A festival calendar and how to congratulate people
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: get to know some festivals. You don't need to memorise everything; it's a basis for conversation. STEP 2: for set dates, use short formulas: «¡Feliz Navidad!», «¡Feliz Año Nuevo!», «¡Felices fiestas!» (Happy holidays!), «¡Feliz cumpleaños!». STEP 3: for an achievement (passing an exam, good news), use «¡Enhorabuena!» (Spain) or «¡Felicidades!» / «¡Felicitaciones!» (very common in Latin America). Don't use «enhorabuena» for a birthday. STEP 4: to wish someone well, use «que» + subjunctive, with the verb right after: «Que lo pases bien.» (Have a good time.), «Que disfrutes de las fiestas.», «Que tengas un buen viaje.» (Have a good trip.) It's the same subjunctive of wishing from lesson 43. STEP 5: «Ojalá» also expresses a wish and takes the subjunctive: «Ojalá haga buen tiempo.» (I hope the weather's good.) STEP 6: the date of a festival takes the article and no preposition: «El 6 de enero», «el último miércoles de agosto», «el uno y el dos de noviembre» — English "ON 6 January" has no equivalent preposition.
blocos.comparacao: English "Congratulations!" splits in two: «¡Enhorabuena!» or «¡Felicidades!» for an achievement, «¡Feliz cumpleaños!» for a birthday. "Have a good time / a good trip" is «Que lo pases bien», «Que tengas buen viaje» (que + subjunctive). And beware: «aniversario» is only an anniversary (of a wedding, an event); a birthday is «cumpleaños».

tabela.quando e onde: Valencia, in March, peaking on the 19th (San José)
tabela.o que se faz: Huge artistic figures are built and then burnt on the last night.

tabela.quando e onde: Buñol (Valencia), on the last Wednesday of August
tabela.o que se faz: Participants throw tomatoes at each other.
There are «encierros», when the bulls run through the streets; many people wear white with a red scarf.

tabela.quando e onde: Many cities in Spain, in March or April
tabela.o que se faz: Processions with religious statues go through the streets.
People eat one grape with each of the twelve chimes of midnight.
On the evening before there are parades, and on the day children get presents; people eat «roscón de Reyes».
People set up altars with photos, flowers and food to remember those who have died.

erros.motivo: «Enhorabuena» is for achievements and good news.
A wish with «que» takes the subjunctive.

blocos.enunciado: Choose a festival from the table and explain out loud: where, when and what people do. End with a congratulation or wish that suits it.
Conjugate «soler» in the present from memory and say a sentence with «solemos».
